key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic equations and shows that the indirect approach admits a conditional error decomposition and residual-based reliability estimate.
engineering_relevance: This gives computational engineers a more principled way to solve PDE-constrained boundary control problems with neural networks while quantifying when soft-constraint PINNs are trustworthy.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control minimize a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control satisfy the optimality system with soft state-control and boundary/terminal constraints.
Error analysis: decompose total error into approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint terms, then derive local stability and residual-to-error bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems—a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear case with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint—to illustrate direct vs. indirect behavior.
watch_item: The reliability guarantee is conditional: it depends on regularity, approximability, bounded soft-constraint residuals, and staying in a local neighborhood of the reference solution.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
